# mabinogi-014 — review

## Pass 1 (2026-11-15)

All 150 units read against the packet's established text and establishment log: every mutation, tense/mood/person
and conjugated-preposition label in the notes; `l` word by word against the Welsh (omissions, additions, order);
`l` against `i` in sense and force; `i` rebuilt from the Welsh where a phrase looked remembered; house renderings
(conventions.md) and the formulas and names as rendered in 001 and 011–013 (Duw a dalho, Sef a wnaeth, Dygaf y Duw
uyg kyffes, derw, trydyd …, hutlath, teulu, Llaw Gyffes, Arglwydes, answer-by-verb); every establishment-log item
is present in its unit's note (all are: a wnaet hi, ady, no [y] before wahawd, no [heb ef], hyhitheu/wedy, agheu,
yn hynn, y glan, y auon, Bryn, ni wybydir, blaen, the second and third englynion, medur, no [eu], hutlath, y'r
ulwydyn, yngynnatau, a'y gwledychwys, the two expunged t's, the dotted o of guybot, canys, [ac ef], i'm byryawd,
yrof i, ymellwng, Trymuryt, anhygar, Yn gyn gyflymet, Nantllew). The Red Book (Rhŷs & Evans 1905) was read for the
whole passage. Evans page images viewed (PyMuPDF, zoom 5): col. 105 ll. 1–14 (o auyr, y auon), col. 106 ll. 1–14
(neita), col. 109 ll. 18–33 (gaffant, Blodeuwed), col. 110 ll. 9–24 (y dyuot, seuiṭ, anniweir). No `t` was touched;
the 150 `t`s are asserted unchanged and no `p` field was added. Edits made by script
(scratchpad r1/edit.py, edit2.py).

### Changes
- 42 · n, l · major · derw was called "commonly taken as its present subjunctive" of daruot; it is deryw, the 3 sg. present with perfect sense, as part 013 already glosses A derw (Red Book same form); `l` "What befalls" did not show that · note rewritten to match 013; `l` "What has-befallen to-you".
- 74 · n · major · "glin soft-mutated after neill": glin is the radical (soft form lin, as in ar lin Gwydyon, unit 108) · corrected; noted that neill leaves it unmutated as it leaves troet.
- 74 · n · major · neita labelled "the 3rd singular imperfect" of neidyaw; the imperfect is neitei and -a is no ordinary ending (image: neita; Red Book neitta) · relabelled a 3 sg. form of uncertain tense.
- 124 · n · major · caffant labelled "present subjunctive" of cael; it is the present indicative (future sense); the subjunctive is the Red Book's caffont (image: gaffant) · corrected, with the Red Book reading.
- 124, 125, 127 · l, i, n · major · the owl passage rendered the name Blodeuedd, so that `i` 125 said "Blodeuedd is the word for 'owl'", which is not what the text says: the text names the owl Blodeuwed, and the -wed form is the point (drafter's flag) · where the text speaks of the name itself and of the owl (124 dy alw … yn Blodeuwed, 125, 127) `l` and `i` now write Blodeuwedd; the person stays Blodeuedd elsewhere (118 included); note 124 says so; its gloss yn Blodeuwed 'as Blodeuwedd'.
- 140 · n · minor · y dyuot glossed 'said' but not called a slip (drafter's flag); image confirms ẏdẏuot with u; Red Book y dywawt · note now says plainly it is a scribal slip for dywot, kept as written and glossed under the intended word.
- 120 · n · minor · the note brought in "Llyn y Morwynion" from tradition; the text does not name the lake · removed; the note says only that the text does not name it.
- 136 · n · minor · the note asserted "each member is 'the third'" and "of the Island of Britain", neither in the text · rewritten on the model of 012's trydyd anuat ergyt: 'the third (of three)', one of a set of three; the other two not named.
- 136 · l · minor · teulu given as "warband" in `l`; house `l` is "household-troop" (`i` keeps "Warbands") · `l` "the third faithless household-troop".
- 63 · n · minor · auyr presented as certainly "the plural of gafr"; more likely gafr with the helping vowel y (cf. pebyr, parabyl, paladyr here), the plural being usually geifyr (drafter's flag) · note now gives both and says which is uncertain; image reading recorded.
- 139 · n · minor · seui labelled the 3 sg. imperfect without qualification (Red Book seuif) · "apparently the 3 sg. imperfect; the form is unusual".
- 139 · n · minor · "ef here is Lleu, the object" stated as certain; ef may equally be the subject (Gronw) · hedged; the sense is the same.
- 106 · n, l · minor · "idaw here marks the eagle as the one who does it" stated as certain; it may be 'down to him' (Gwydion); `l` had "by-him" for idaw · both readings given; `l` "to-him".
- 10 · l, i · minor · y gwn rendered "the hounds", but the note rightly says cwn is soft-mutated after y 'his' (the article would not mutate a plural) · "his hounds" in `l` and `i`.
- 12 · l · minor · y wlat arall 'to another land' (y 'to', no article) rendered "to the other land" · "to another land".
- 2 · l · minor · lef corn "the cry of-a-horn": no article · "a-cry of-a-horn".
- 6 · n · minor · Pebyr glossed 'radiant, bright, strong'; pefr is not 'strong' · "strong" dropped.
- 54 · l · minor · wnay (present 'will make') given as "would-make" · "will-make" (`i`'s conditional English kept, from metrei).
- 70 · i · minor · bwch is 'he-goat'; `i` said "called goats" · "called he-goats".
- 98 · l · minor · gwrthwyneb auon 'the opposite of a river' given as "against the river" · "taking the-opposite of-a-river".
- 98 · i · minor · guastatau rendered "slowed" in `i` against "halting" in `l` and the note's 'come to a stand' · "came to rest".
- 99 · l · minor · yn y bori 'grazing it': the y 'it' was dropped in `l` · "grazing-it".
- 105 · n · minor · Llaw Gyffes glossed "usually taken as 'deft, sure'", out of step with 013 ('Steady Hand') (drafter's flag) · "'steady, sure' as in part 013".
- 108 · l, i, n · minor · hutlath "magic staff", where 012 has "magic rod" · "magic-rod" / "magic rod".
- 85 · n · minor · y Maynawr: the hedge stood without the evidence (drafter's flag) · added that the Red Book has ym maenawr.
- 97 · n · minor · a'y canlynwys glossed with infixed 'her' without saying the expected spirant mutation (chanlynwys) is not written · added.
- 124 · l · minor · yn before the name not shown · "your calling ever as Blodeuwedd".
- 130 · i · minor · the oath y Duw dygaf uyg kyffes rendered "as I make my confession to God"; 011/013 render the formula as its own clause · "I will not take it; I make my confession to God".
- 21 · l · style · llywenyd "joy" here, "gladness" in 16 (and in `i`) · "great gladness".
- 88 · l · style · "in tonight" reverses heno y mywn · "tonight in".
- 104 · l · style · ynteu yr eryr reordered · "he-for-his-part the eagle".
- 131 · l · style · ohonaw ef moved forward · restored to Welsh order ("to the place I-was by-him").
- 128 · n · style · yngynnatau's ym- called "reflexive" · "the prefix ym-".

### Refused
- 47, 134, 136, 143 ergyt 'cast' (drafter's flag): kept. It is a spear throw here, and keeping 'blow' for dyrnawt (house) lets 140's dyrnawt and 143's ergyt stay distinct as the text has them.
- 56 y hanuones, 97 y hegyr (h-forms; drafter's flag): the notes already say "probably the infixed pronoun" and give the alternative; the Red Book has the same h-forms. Left as they are.
- 59 `l` "[yn hynn]": marking the doubtful Welsh in `l` is the practice of the englynion units (107) and of 012's "daran(?)"; the note says what is uncertain. Kept.
- 103, 105, 107 `l` "An-oak that-grows" against `i` "An oak grows": Dar a dyf can be read either way (abnormal sentence or relative); the englynion are marked tentative throughout. Not changed.
- 98 Nantlleu: the modern place-name is Nantlle, but the text's point is 'Lleu's valley' and the note explains Nantllew; changing it to Nantlle would bring in outside knowledge the text does not give. Kept; the owner may rule.
- 18, 100, 104, 118 `l` "That-is what did X" (verb before subject) where 011–013 write "That-is what X did:": both follow the house "That-is"; this part's order is closer to the Welsh. Not normalised.
- 28 `i` "be together for good": interpretive but faithful to the plotting; kept.
- 12 yn goganu as 'our reviling' (it could be progressive yn + verbal noun): the note's reading gives good sense; not changed.
- 6, 78, 85 short geographical glosses (Penllyn round Llyn Tegid, Ardudwy in Meirionnydd, Arfon facing Môn): factual locating notes of the kind earlier parts carry, not readings of the text; kept, unlike 120's lake-name, which put a traditional name on something the text leaves unnamed.
